answer: An operator running many aliases therefore pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the dune quota and the vault admission check. Submission rate is limited to 8 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. Because the counters live in the relic ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
